$comment: Single source of truth for the UV-1601 digital twin: TrojanUVSwiftSC D12 closed-vessel UV reactor with 12 LPHO amalgam lamps for drinking-water disinfection. Reactor data from the Trojan brochure; dose requirements, lamp data and alarms from the US EPA UVDGM.

twin.kind: Closed-vessel UV disinfection reactor (drinking water) with UV sensors, UVT analyser and automatic wiper

standards.performance: TrojanUVSwiftSC D12: 12 LPHO amalgam lamps, DVGW-validated 40 mJ/cm2, UVT 70-98 %, 1-40 C, 10 bar, DN300, 2 UV sensors, variable ballasts 60-100 %, automatic wiper
standards.dose: Calculated-dose approach (US EPA UVDGM): RED = K (S/S0) G(UVA) / Q with the sensor intensity S, UV absorbance UVA and flow Q; equation form and constant are this twin's calibration, not Trojan's validation equation
standards.credit: Log inactivation from US EPA UVDGM Table 1.4 (40 CFR 141.720(d)(1)); off-specification rule: >= 95 % of the monthly volume within validated conditions (40 CFR 141.720(d)(3))
standards.information_model: Points named after the controller's Modbus / PROFINET I/O (UV intensity, lamp status, power level, wiper)

identification.location: UV building / train 1, after the filters

reactor.lamp_kw_note: 320 W per lamp assumed (UVDGM Table 2.1: LPHO 1.5-10 W/cm)
reactor.dimensions_note: Trojan drawing letters A-F for D12; used for the 3D proportions

validation.assumed: flow limit 800 m3/h and minimum UVT 80 % for this unit are assumptions (Trojan publishes the family range only)

dose_model.note: Kc set so that the design flow at 94 % UVT gets 40 mJ/cm2 at the end-of-lamp-life and fouling factors (0.80 x 0.90)

lamp_ageing.law: linear output loss to 0.80 at 12,000 h
lamp_ageing.basis: UVDGM Table 2.1 LPHO 8,000-12,000 h; Ushio amalgam lamps: 20 % degradation over > 16,000 h. 0.80 at 12,000 h is this twin's (conservative) assumption

credit_table.source: US EPA UVDGM Table 1.4 / 40 CFR 141.720(d)(1); log credit read between the table points, capped at 4

demo.note: The plant clock runs 60x real time: lamp hours advance one hour per real minute (the lamps are replaced at 11,000 h automatically), a month of volume counters is 12 real hours, and the trapped water heats to the trip in a few minutes when the flow stops.

points.label: Flow through the reactor (dedicated flow meter)
UV transmittance at 254 nm, 1 cm (online UVT analyser)
Reactor: 0 disinfecting, 1 alarm, 2 shut down (high temperature)

lamp_failure.label: Lamp / ballast failure (lamps out)
lamp_failure.cause: A lamp or its ballast fails: the lamp group loses output, the sensor watching it drops and the controller turns the other lamps up (dose pacing). Two lamps out at full severity
lamp_failure.action: Replace the lamp (and ballast if it is the cause); check the sleeve is not cracked

lamp_end_of_life.label: Lamps past end of life
lamp_end_of_life.cause: Lamp hours run past the validated 12,000 h: output falls below the end-of-lamp-life factor the dose was validated with
lamp_end_of_life.action: Replace all 12 lamps; reset the lamp-hour counter

sleeve_fouling.label: Sleeve fouling (wiper failure)
sleeve_fouling.cause: The wiper drive stalls; hardness and iron/manganese deposit on the warm quartz sleeves: less UV reaches the water at the same lamp power and UVT
sleeve_fouling.action: Repair the wiper drive; clean the sleeves chemically; check feed hardness / Fe / Mn

uvt_drop.label: Feed UVT drop (water quality)
uvt_drop.cause: Raw water changes (rain, algae, humic matter): the water absorbs more UV. Intensity falls but exactly as the UVT explains - the reactor is fine, the water is not
uvt_drop.action: Check the upstream treatment (coagulation, filtration); the reactor runs at full power; consider reducing flow

sensor_drift.label: UV sensor drift
sensor_drift.cause: Sensor 1 window or photodiode ages: it reads low while sensor 2 and the twin's expectation do not - the controller wastes power pacing up
sensor_drift.action: Check sensor 1 against the reference sensor; clean the window or replace and recalibrate

ballast_fault.label: Ballast / power supply fault
ballast_fault.cause: A ballast overheats and derates: the lamps draw less power than the controller commands, and the heat-sink runs hot
ballast_fault.action: Check the control panel cooling and the ballast; replace the ballast board

high_flow.label: Flow above the validated range
high_flow.cause: Another reactor trips or demand jumps: this reactor carries more than its validated flow, residence time and dose fall
high_flow.action: Bring a standby reactor on line or throttle the flow; count the off-specification volume

no_flow_overheat.label: No flow, lamps on (overheating)
no_flow_overheat.cause: An isolation valve closes while the lamps stay on: the trapped water heats up until the high-temperature trip shuts the lamps down (risk to sleeves and water hammer on restart)
no_flow_overheat.action: Interlock the lamps with the flow; let the reactor cool before restart; vent and refill slowly

compare.label: UV dose (validated, from sensors)
compare.basis: measured: lower sensor, UVT, flow; expected: lamp age and power, clean sleeves

compare.label: UV intensity (mean of 2 sensors)
compare.basis: S0 250 W/m² × power × age factor × clean sleeve 0.97 × UVT³ (3 cm water)

design.label: Reactor
design.value: TrojanUVSwiftSC D12: 12 LPHO amalgam lamps, DVGW 40 mJ/cm², UVT 70-98 %, DN300, 316L, 10 bar

design.label: Assumed
design.value: 320 W per lamp, max 800 m³/h, min UVT 80 %, design 650 m³/h at 94 %, fouling 0.90, EOLL 0.80

design.label: Credit
design.value: US EPA UVDGM Table 1.4: 12 mJ/cm² = 3-log Cryptosporidium; 95 % monthly volume rule

design.label: Source
design.value: TrojanUVSwiftSC brochure; US EPA UVDGM 2006; 3D built from Trojan's published dimensions, not manufacturer CAD
